summary: Redwood AE/SE ran a hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking for SkyRocket's search product. Key topics: integration patterns (embed -> vector DB -> rerank), sample latency & cost tradeoffs, security (SOC2, KMS, VPC/private), and next steps to run a short POC with a 1M doc sample.
topics: Console demo: metrics and cost breakdowns
transcript:
[00:00] Meeting header: 2028-06-02 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jared Lee (Redwood SE), Anil Patel (CTO - SkyRocket), Sofia Martinez (Search Eng), Liam O'Connor (Product), Nora Kim (Eng Manager)

[00:08] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, i'll kick us off, jared will run the deeper tech bits. you all good with agenda?
[00:16] Anil: yea, sounds good, thanks. quick note—we're interested in embeddings + rerank for our primary search product, latency under 120ms ideally for top doc rerank, cost is also a big factor.
[00:30] Maya: perfect, we'll show a two stage workflow — dense retrieval + redwood's rerank endpoint to get high precision. we'll also show the console so you can see token-level cost and latency.
[00:45] Jared: okay i'll start with the api shapes, there's an embeddings endpoint that returns 1536-d vectors by default for the base model, but we support 1024/2048 tradeoffs and quantized variants. note: we sometimes call out model names slightly different in the docs, so sorry if you see redwoood in there, small typos lurk.
[01:10] Sofia: 1536 is what we're using now, on a mix of product docs & user queries. curious about vector size -> recall tradeoffs and storage cost.
[01:25] Jared: yeah, storage roughly linear, 1536 floats is about X bytes, if you quantize to int8 you're roughly 4x smaller. latency wise, on hosted we do batching and kv-cache for generate calls, but for embeddings it's a single-pass so it's pretty fast — usually 5-20ms per embed depending on concurrency.
[01:45] Liam: how do you typically integrate with vector dbs like pinecone or elastic? do you recommend pushing everything into your dedicated storage?
[01:55] Maya: most customers use Redwood hosted embeddings + their vector DB of choice. we don't force storage, we return vectors and metadata. we also provide a sample rerank call that takes candidate ids + original query + context and returns a re-ordered list or score deltas.
[02:18] Anil: ok show us a demo flow, would like to see actual payloads and timings.

-- Demo starts --
[02:30] Jared: i'll share screen; here's a notebook—step one: call POST /v1/embeddings with body {"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":[...]} returns vectors. step two: store in vec db. step three: search to get top K candidates then call POST /v1/rerank with {"model":"redwood-rerank-1","query":"...","candidates":[{id:..., text:...}, ...]}. note the rerank endpoint is optimized for short-context cross-encoder style scoring so it does full attention across query+doc snippets.
[03:10] Maya: and just to clarify, rerank costs are per candidate token + query tokens — the console breaks that down so you can see which route is expensive.
[03:25] Sofia: what's a typical latency for rerank on hosted? say K=10?
[03:30] Jared: depends on model and sequence lengths, for our mid-tier rerank model we see ~60-110ms p99 for K=10 in the hosted region eu-west. on faster configs it hits ~30-60ms. so you're in the ballpark of your 120ms target if you size appropriately.
[03:50] Anil: what's the throughput? we expect spikes around product launches.
[03:56] Maya: hosted is multi-tenant with autoscaling, but if you need predictable throughput we recommend Dedicated (reserved GPU pools). for spikes we have burst capacity options and auto-fallback to cheaper model variants if primary is constrained.
[04:12] Liam: can we see the console for metrics?
[04:15] Jared: jumping to console — here's a route dashboard: token-level cost, avg latency, p50/p95/p99, and per-model breakdown. if you scroll you can enable tracing hooks to link a trace id back to your application logs.
[04:35] Anil: nice, can we set alerts on quality regressions?
[04:38] Maya: yes, Redwood Optimize hooks let you tie eval prompt sets and regression alerts; you'll get diffs when a new model or config degrades recall/precision.
[04:50] Sofia: security — do you have SOC2, SSO, and KMS? we have strict compliance, and need to ensure logs are auditable.
[04:58] Maya: we have SOC 2 Type II, support SAML/SSO, and integrate with customer KMS providers. For Private deployments we support VPC peering and on-prem air-gapped options; audit logs are available at route-level with retention options. i'll share the security pack after the call.
[05:18] Anil: what about data residency? we have EU-only data requirements.
[05:21] Jared: hosted regions include eu-west, us-east, ap-southeast. we can pin your account to eu-only regions; for stricter needs customers choose Private.
[05:32] Liam: show us a sample rerank scoring output — i want to see explainability.
[05:38] Jared: here's an example response: [{"id":123,"score":0.92,"explanation":"query overlap + semantic relevance"}, ...] — explanation is heuristics + token-level attention highlights in the console, though it's not deterministic like a full LLM chain explanation, it's useful for debugging. (note: explanation strings sometimes truncated by the auto transcript).
[06:05] Sofia: are you doing on-the-fly token caching for rerank? we'd like to avoid recomputing for repeated queries.
[06:12] Jared: rerank is a cross-encoder so cache patterns are trickier than for autoregressive generation. we do candidate-level caching and suggestions around prefix caching for generative flows. for dense retrieval+rerank you usually cache embeddings and frequently-seen candidate scores depending on staleness windows.

[06:40] Maya: let's run a quick live example — i'll paste a sample query and jared will run embed+search+rerank on a small sample set we preloaded.
[06:48] Jared: executing... embed call 12ms, vector search top10 returned, rerank call p50 ~ 45ms in this region. results reordered — original top had some spammy matches, rerank boosted the context-rich doc.
[07:15] Anil: that reorder looks promising. do you have any hard numbers on cost per query at K=10?
[07:22] Maya: rough ballpark for mid-tier model: embeddings ~0.2c per 1K queries? hmm sorry, that was off — numbers are in the pricing sheet, i'll send exact per-1000-embed and per-rerank-candidate costs. console also shows per-route cost so you can attribute spend to product areas.
[07:50] Liam: one friction is our infra team prefers fewer external calls. they'd rather send batched requests or run dedicated. how invasive is the integration?
[07:58] Jared: API is simple REST/SDKs; typical integration is 2-4 days to get embeddings flowing, another week for rerank tuning. if you want less external dependency, Dedicated or Private options reduce network hops and you can run inside your VPC.
[08:15] Anil: have you done similar POCs for companies our size?
[08:20] Maya: yes, several search-first SaaS (we've worked with Brightfind, NovaSearch, etc.) we can share anonymized benchmarks.
[08:30] Nora: about data retention — we need guarantee that customer data is not used for model training.
[08:35] Maya: hosted has opt-out for training and we have contracts that guarantee data not used for model training for enterprise customers; Private deployments keep data fully customer-controlled. i'll attach the legal clause.

-- Deep technical digressions --
[09:00] Jared: quick note on quantization: if you move to int8 you get big storage/cost wins but some small recall drop depending on models; Optimize can recommend quant profiles per workload. also kernel selection matters for long sequences, our runtime picks the best CUDA kernel and uses continuous batching to hide GPU latency.
[09:35] Sofia: would you help us pick embedding dimensions and similarity metric? we're between cosine vs dot product.
[09:42] Jared: cosine for most semantic tasks, dot product sometimes for productized ranking if vectors are normalized differently. we'll run A/B tests in the POC.
[09:55] Anil: networking question — if we do a private deployment in our k8s, how much operational lift? we have a small infra team.
[10:02] Maya: Private requires some infra work but our deploy package includes helm charts and an ops runbook. we also offer a managed Private where we help with initial setup for a professional services fee.

[10:20] Liam: any gotchas around idempotency or candidate ordering? we need stable results for logged reproductions.
[10:26] Jared: rerank is deterministic per model + seed; however if you update model version you'll see differences. Console's rollout features let you canary model changes and do A/B tests with automatic fallback.

[10:45] Maya: ok, questions from the product side?
[10:48] Liam: is the rerank endpoint able to take metadata like click signals as features?
[10:53] Jared: yes you can pass additional features per candidate and we support hybrid scoring (learned + feature-based weights). this is configured in the rerank payload. small note: some field names in the older docs may show mismatched casing.

[11:10] Anil: can we run a benchmark on our 1M doc set? timeline?
[11:15] Maya: yes, for hosted we can run a staged benchmark with your sample queries, usually 1-2 weeks for meaningful results; if you want faster we can do a small sample and extrapolate.
[11:25] Nora: cost wise we need an estimate for monthly run at our expected query volume (~10M queries/month).
[11:31] Maya: we'll model that once you give sample QPS distribution, we'll include embed + search + rerank in the costing sheet.

[11:45] Jared: quick note on privacy: for EU-only, we'll pin region and disable cross-region failover unless you opt in. for HIPAA customers we have additional business associate agreements.

[12:05] Maya: wrapping up — recap and next steps. we'll send pricing + SLA, security pack, a demo notebook, and provision a trial API key loaded with a small sample of your data for benchmarking. schedule POC kickoff next Mon/Wed?
[12:25] Anil: Wed morning works.
[12:28] Sofia: please include our infra lead in the kickoff invite.
[12:31] Maya: absolutely.
[12:34] Liam: thanks everyone — this was useful.
[12:36] Maya: thanks all; action items are in the notes, we'll follow up by EOD with docs and invites.

[12:45] End meeting.
